subject: Tenant uptime discrepancy — request for downtime validation and credit proposal
messages:
From: Ari Goodman <ari@greenlinepay.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: account-ops@greenlinepay.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Tenant uptime anomaly — request for downtime confirmation and credit

Hi Vivek / Jonas,

We observed a sustained availability drop for our tenant (glp-payments-prod) early this morning. Our internal monitoring measured about 4.5% unavailable time across the 03:00–04:00 UTC hour (spikes of 503s and connection resets). Can Redwood confirm whether this qualifies as downtime under our SLA and — if so — provide a preliminary credit estimate?

What we've attached: a heatmap from our edge (downtime-heatmap.png) and a short trace bundle (we'll upload full traces if you need them). Our billing month runs UTC 1st–30th. This incident, per our telemetry, impacted checkout throughput and led to ~2.1% revenue loss for the hour.

Immediate asks:
- Confirm whether this period is counted as service downtime in your telemetry (we saw 03:12:15–03:38:42 UTC as the most severe window).
- If eligible, rough credit % / $ that we should expect while you do a full postmortem.
- ETA for a postmortem and log bundle.

We appreciate a fast confirmation — finance is already queuing an adjustment request pending your verification.

Thanks,
Ari Goodman
Director, Platform Reliability
GreenLine Payments

Attachments: downtime-heatmap.png (image), prod-traces-2026-11-25.zip (partial)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Goodman <ari@greenlinepay.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Tenant uptime anomaly — request for downtime confirmation and credit

Ari — thanks for the heads up and for the artifacts. I've routed this to SRE for an immediate correlation pass and asked product telemetry to pull the canonical availability window.

Quick notes / next steps:
- SRE (cc'd internally) will reconcile the edge heatmap against our control-plane and serving runtime logs.
- If the 03:12–03:38 UTC window is confirmed as an availability loss for your tenant, our SLA Appendix A (monthly uptime) would apply; I'll ask Jonas to draft a provisional credit calc for that window.
- Please send the full trace bundle (Link or Drive) if you haven't already — that speeds the evidence pull.

Provisional response: we can provide an initial estimate within the next 4 business hours. If eligible, we'll propose a proportional credit only for the impacted hour rather than a full-day proration — that tends to match the contract language for multi-tenant disruptions.

I'll follow up once SRE returns the reconciled downtime window.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

[Attachment request: full-trace-bundle, logs requested: serving-logs-2026-11-26 (shard 7)]
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 12:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Tenant uptime anomaly — request for downtime confirmation and credit

Vivek / Laura — SRE validated an impact window that largely overlaps with the customer's telemetry. Summary below (internal):

*Verified window:* 2026-11-26 03:11:58 UTC — 2026-11-26 03:39:14 UTC (approx. 27m 16s).
*Root cause snapshot:* transient overload on a serving pool due to a mis-sized autoscaler cooldown; KV-cache pressure increased tail latency causing a subset of requests to fail with 503s. We saw repeated preemption/requeue cycles for the tenant's shard group during that interval.

SLA math (quick, provisional):
- Contracted monthly uptime: 99.95% (Appendix A, section 3.2.1).
- Minutes in month (UTC Nov): 30 * 24 * 60 = 43,200.
- Allowed downtime per month: 0.05% * 43,200 = 21.6 minutes.
- Customer observed ~27.3 minutes (exceeds allowance by ~5.7 minutes).

Proposed credit calc (per Appendix A):
- Exceeded minutes: 5.7 -> proportional credit bucket.
- For exceeded window we recommend a credit equal to 10% of the monthly recurring fee pro-rated for the exceeded minutes, capped by contract terms.

Operational asks:
1) We need the customer's billing contact to issue a formal credit notice.
2) Prepare a short-form postmortem (one pager + timeline + mitigation) for the customer within 5 business days.
3) Offer a one-time engineering review with their integration team (if they request).

Attachments (internal): internal-trace-sample-shard7.log (we'll push full bundle to Drive). I've flagged this for an expedited postmortem and included a suggested email for the customer that Vivek can send (formalizes the credit path).

Jonas
Principal Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Maya Patel <maya.patel@greenlinepay.com>
Accounts Payable — GreenLine Payments

Ari
